Maintenance Report — MNT-0181-006

Asset: WELL-0181 (NE-08 Well 181, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 27 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Nov 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 255 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0181-0054 on 2023-10-26 Report written: 07 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0181-0054 showed the wellhead at 21.9 °C with the air at 21.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Consumables1,979

Total32,053

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0181-008

Asset: WELL-0181 (NE-08 Well 181, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 Jan 2024 08:00 · Finished: 20 Jan 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0181-0066 on 2024-01-18 Report written: 21 Jan 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0181-0066 at 09:45 on 2024-01-18 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.1% of the pad area, estimated 0.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 238 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 190 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0181-008 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.48% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Line pipe and fittings1,341
Absorbents and berms596
Soil hauling and disposal1,043
Labour (company crew and contractor)3,409
Total6,389

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-04MetPermit issued; gas test 0% LEL
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)
SR-02MetContained about 2.9 hours after discovery (limit 4 hours)
SR-04MetSpill recorded with volume and area (minor class)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0181-011

Asset: WELL-0181 (NE-08 Well 181, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 25 Jun 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 44 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0181-0088 on 2024-06-20 Report written: 25 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0181-0088 showed the wellhead at 35.3 °C with the air at 34.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0181-019

Asset: WELL-0181 (NE-08 Well 181, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: rod string Work started: 03 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 19 Aug 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 384 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0181-0146 on 2025-07-31 Report written: 21 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0181-0146 showed the wellhead at 41.6 °C with the air at 35.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 14 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD

Rod couplings941
Fishing tool rental1,568
Labour (company crew and contractor)6,844
Total13,116

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 3 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
